question: If base perimeter = 40 cm, slant height = 10 cm, what is lateral surface area of square pyramid?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any regular pyramid, the lateral surface area can be calculated directly using its base perimeter and slant height.

Lateral Surface Area = ½ × Base Perimeter × Slant Height

⇒ LSA = ½ × 40 × 10

⇒ LSA = 200 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 200 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base perimeter = 40 cm

Slant height (l) = 10 cm

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
 
 l = 10 cm
 a = 10 cm
 Base Perimeter = 40 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of one lateral triangle = ½ × Base × Slant height

Side of square base (a) = Perimeter ÷ 4

**Calculation:**

⇒ Side of the base (a) = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 cm

⇒ A square pyramid has 4 identical lateral triangular faces.

⇒ Area of one triangular face = ½ × 10 × 10

⇒ Area of one triangular face = 50 cm²

⇒ Total Lateral Surface Area = 4 × Area of one face

⇒ Total LSA = 4 × 50 = 200 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 200 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The TSA of a regular pyramid is the sum of its Lateral Surface Area and Base Area. For a square pyramid of base side 'a': TSA = LSA + a².

Volume of a Pyramid

The volume of any pyramid is one-third of the product of its base area and true vertical height. V = ⅓ × Base Area × h.

Relation between Heights

For a regular square pyramid, the true vertical height (h), slant height (l), and base side (a) form a right-angled triangle. By Pythagoras theorem: l² = h² + (a/2)².
